description: Experience the rich, creamy indulgence of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani, a beloved Indian classic. Tender chicken pieces are simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of tanginess and mild sweetness, making it an irresistible choice for any meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary, to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and slightly charred on the edges. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter. Add the chopped onion and saute until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, crushed green cardamoms, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then add the soaked cashews. Cover and cook on low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes are cooked down and the oil begins to separate.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamoms (if desired, for a smoother gravy). Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. If the gravy is too thick, add a little water to achieve desired consistency. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Add the sugar and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Cook for 2-3 minutes more without boiling, just until heated through and creamy. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro. Serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice for a delicious Indian lunch.

tips: For a truly authentic taste, slightly char the marinated chicken under a broiler or in a very hot pan to mimic the smoky flavor of a tandoor oven before adding to the gravy.

Always use good quality, ripe tomatoes or canned crushed tomatoes for the gravy base to achieve a rich color and deep flavor. Soaking cashews beforehand is crucial for a perfectly smooth and creamy gravy.
Serve Butter Chicken hot with freshly baked naan, jeera rice, or plain basmati rice. Garnish generously with fresh cilantro and a swirl of extra cream for an inviting presentation.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is more than just a dish; it's an experience. A culinary icon from India, this creamy, rich, and subtly spiced curry has captivated palates worldwide, cementing its place as one of the most beloved Indian lunch recipes. If you've ever savored its velvety texture and tender chicken, you'll understand why Butter Chicken holds such a special spot in the hearts of food lovers. Often gracing the menus of fine Indian restaurants, Murgh Makhani, as it's traditionally known, is surprisingly achievable in your home kitchen. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create an authentic and irresistible version of this classic dish.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?
Murgh Makhani, literally translating to "chicken with butter," is famously known as Butter Chicken. This iconic dish originated in the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. The story goes that the chefs, needing to use up leftover tandoori chicken, simmered it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was an instant sensation.

At its heart, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani features succulent pieces of chicken (often marinated in yogurt and spices, then grilled or pan-fried) swimming in a luxurious, vibrant orange-red sauce. This sauce is a masterful blend of pureed tomatoes, ginger, garlic, aromatic spices like garam masala and fenugreek (kasoori methi), and a generous amount of butter and cream, which impart its signature richness and smooth texture. It’s a dish that perfectly balances tanginess from tomatoes, sweetness, and a mild warmth from spices, making it incredibly approachable even for those new to Indian cuisine. Its universal appeal lies in its comforting creaminess and depth of flavor, making it a perfect hearty and satisfying Indian lunch recipe.

## Ingredients You Need
To create an authentic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani, quality ingredients are key. Here’s a comprehensive list:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   1 kg boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani (Butter Chicken) Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons ghee or unsalted butter, plus more for garnish
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
*   1 kg ripe tomatoes, pureed (or 2 cans 400g crushed tomatoes)
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in warm water for 15 minutes (optional, for extra creaminess)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi), crushed
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh coriander leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Creating this flavorful Indian lunch recipe involves a few key stages:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours for best flavor.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or ghee in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Cook until browned and slightly charred on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. The chicken doesn’t need to be fully cooked through at this stage. Remove chicken and set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, add 2 tablespoons of ghee or butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Add Aromatics and Tomatoes:** Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the pureed tomatoes (or crushed tomatoes), red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the raw tomato smell disappears.
5.  **Blend the Sauce (Optional but Recommended):** For a super smooth sauce, allow the mixture to cool slightly, then transfer it to a blender. If using, add the soaked cashews. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  **Simmer the Makhani:** Return the smooth sauce to the pan over medium heat. Stir in the garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, and sugar.
7.  **Combine and Finish:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, allowing the chicken to cook through and absorb the flavors of the sauce.
8.  **Enrich with Cream and Butter:** Stir in the heavy cream and a knob of butter. Cook for just 2-3 minutes more, ensuring the sauce doesn't boil vigorously after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
9.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish generously with fresh coriander leaves and a swirl of extra cream or a small dollop of butter.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with these expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal for maximum flavor absorption.
*   **Char the Chicken:** If possible, grill or pan-fry the marinated chicken until it gets a slight char. This adds a smoky depth that mimics the tandoor oven and greatly enhances the overall flavor of your Butter Chicken.
*   **Tomato Quality Matters:** Use ripe, good-quality tomatoes for the freshest flavor. If using canned, opt for high-quality crushed or pureed tomatoes for the best results.
*   **Smooth Sauce is Supreme:** Blending the sauce (and straining it) is the secret to that luscious, velvety texture characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. Don't skip this step if you desire an authentic restaurant-style finish. The cashews, when blended, also add to this richness.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Butter Chicken is all about balance. The sugar helps cut the acidity of the tomatoes, while kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves) adds an indispensable earthy, slightly bitter aroma that is characteristic of Murgh Makhani. Don't omit it.
*   **Don't Overcook After Cream:** Once you add the cream, cook for only a couple of minutes on low heat. Boiling vigorously after adding cream can cause it to split, affecting the sauce's texture.

## Serving Suggestions
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when served with traditional Indian accompaniments. Pair it with warm, fluffy naan bread or roti to scoop up every last drop of the exquisite sauce. Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) are also excellent choices for soaking up the rich flavors. For a refreshing contrast, serve a side of cooling cucumber raita (yogurt dip) and a simple kachumber salad (diced onion, tomato, cucumber with lemon dressing).

## Variations and Substitutions
This versatile Indian lunch recipe can be adapted to suit various dietary needs and preferences:

*   **Vegetarian Butter Paneer:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), mushrooms, or mixed vegetables for a delicious vegetarian alternative. Marinate paneer lightly in spices before adding to the sauce.
*   **Vegan Option:** Use plant-based chicken substitutes or extra firm tofu. Replace butter with olive oil or vegan butter, and heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream. Ensure all other ingredients are vegan.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference. For a milder dish, reduce it; for more heat, add finely chopped green chilies or extra chili powder. Kashmiri chili powder is excellent for providing vibrant color without excessive heat.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you don't have a grill, you can achieve a subtle smoky flavor by placing a small piece of burning charcoal in a small heatproof bowl inside the finished curry, drizzling a teaspoon of ghee over it, and quickly covering the pot for a few minutes. This is called 'dhungar' or smoke infusion.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is undoubtedly a crown jewel of Indian cuisine, offering a symphony of flavors that is both comforting and exotic. Its creamy texture, tender chicken, and perfectly balanced sweet and tangy notes make it a universally loved dish. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore new culinary horizons, preparing this classic Indian lunch recipe from scratch is a rewarding experience. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to impress your taste buds and loved ones with a truly unforgettable meal. Enjoy the magic of homemade Butter Chicken!
